name: Ablative Charge Disruption Rifle ACDR-2 'Sandpaper'
description:
The Ablative Charge Disruption Rifle ACDR-2 fires a coherent stream of triboelectrically charged microparticles — each grain roughly 40 microns in diameter — accelerated to moderate velocity through a segmented linear barrel. On contact with a target surface, the particles discharge accumulated static potential simultaneously, creating a combined ablative and electrostatic effect that strips insulating coatings, disrupts surface-mounted electronics, and causes intense localized irritation to exposed biological tissue. It is, in the bluntest terms, a gun that sandpapers things until they stop working.

Arctures Defense Solutions developed the ACDR-2 primarily as an anti-materiel platform for defeating hardened drone carapaces and armored cyberware without requiring explosive munitions in confined spaces. The triboelectric charge buildup during barrel transit is self-generating — the particles charge themselves against the barrel lining, meaning the weapon requires no external charge source beyond the kinetic energy of the propellant. This passive charging mechanism keeps the design mechanically simple and brutally reliable, with fewer failure points than comparable electromagnetic weapons.

The weapon's unpleasant reputation among its users comes from its secondary biological effect. While not designed as an anti-personnel weapon, the microparticle stream causes severe dermabrasion and mucosal irritation at close range, and the electrostatic discharge against cybernetic implants can trigger involuntary motor responses and sensory feedback spikes. Users have described the experience of being hit as feeling like being scrubbed with broken glass that also bites. Field operators have given it the nickname 'Sandpaper' with no affection.
legality: Licensed — registered operators and contracted security; Restricted — civilian
specifications:
effective range: 3–25 meters optimal, degraded beyond 40 meters
particle size: 35–50 microns, variable by canister load
muzzle velocity: 320 m/s particle stream
power source: Kinetic self-charging barrel lining, standard propellant cell
weight: 3.8 kg with standard canister
canister capacity: 80 bursts per canister
anti-materiel effectiveness: Rated for hardened polymer carapace and Grade 2 cyberware coating
form factor: Bullpup carbine configuration with swappable canister breech
tactical_use: Used in drone interdiction, anti-cyberware engagements, and close-quarters breaching where explosive munitions create unacceptable collateral risk. Operators typically sweep exposed drone joints and sensor clusters before engaging with primary weapons. In anti-personnel roles, targeting cybernetic limbs and implant housings forces opponents to manage involuntary feedback responses, creating openings for secondary engagement. Requires operators to wear particle filtration masks, as backscatter in enclosed spaces can irritate users' own respiratory systems.
cultural_context: Among cyberware-heavy communities in GLMZ, the ACDR-2 is regarded with particular contempt — it targets the augmentations people have sacrificed to obtain, treating expensive bodily investment as a vulnerability. Getting 'sandpapered' is used as slang for having your identity systematically eroded by institutional forces. Ironically, the weapon is also used by anti-augmentation extremist groups who have obtained black market units, giving it an uncomfortable political double meaning. Legitimate security contractors who use it often face hostility from aug-positive communities even when deployment is legally sanctioned.
known_users: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS field demonstration teams
'Grit' — a freelance wrecker known for disabling cyberware before negotiations
story_hooks: A series of attacks on aug-clinic workers have been carried out with ACDR-2s traced back to a legitimate security contractor — someone is using licensed weapons for ideologically motivated violence and covering it with paperwork.

A new canister load has appeared on the black market with particles sized to penetrate cybernetic housing seals rather than just strip coatings — essentially turning the weapon into a cyberware killer.
An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the 'self-charging' barrel mechanism has a secondary function that records electrostatic signatures of every cyberware system it hits, feeding a biometric database.
A player character's expensive new cyberlimb has been flagged as having a coating composition that makes it uniquely vulnerable to ACDR-2 fire — and someone knows it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact bullpup carbine with an aggressive, industrial aesthetic. The barrel assembly dominates the upper profile—a segmented, ribbed tube with visible electrode bands spiraling along its length. The weapon reads as purpose-built and utilitarian, all hard angles and functional geometry with no concessions to ergonomics or aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 68 cm | Barrel length: 38 cm | Width across grip: 7 cm | Height (with rail mounts): 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—3.8 kg distributed across the bullpup frame creates a weapon that feels substantial without being unwieldy. The segmented barrel adds perceived weight forward without the actual burden.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened polymer composite frame with brushed titanium alloy barrel segments and steel internal assembly. The breech block and magazine well are reinforced steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with burnished steel barrel segments showing subtle oxidation patina. The electrode bands are bare brushed titanium with faint electrical scoring marks from repeated charge cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray and charcoal black primary, with silver titanium barrel accents. Faint copper-orange corrosion blooming at electrode contact points.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized textured polymer, deeply knurled to accommodate gloved hands. Slight tacky residue from particle discharge buildup—users rarely fully clean this weapon.
distinctive_features: Segmented barrel with visible helical electrode bands spaced 8mm apart
Static discharge indicator strip along the right side—changes color under electrostatic load
Swappable canister breech with bayonet-style locking tabs
Ventilation slots along the barrel shroud to dissipate triboelectric heat
Iron Point Ammunition 'IP' logo stamped on the dust cover, partially worn
Custom operator callsigns scratched or burned into the polymer stock by field users
Faint white particulate residue caked around the muzzle crown and venting ports
Integrated particle filtration intake vent near the trigger guard
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Iron Point Ammunition logo (stylized iron claw) stamped on the upper receiver. Serial plate on the left side of the breech block. Warning labels for electrostatic discharge in Mandarin and English stamped on the magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Battle-worn with heavy use marks. The barrel segments show scorching and micro-fracturing from repeated charge cycles. Grip tape is worn through in places. The polymer stock bears impact scars and burn marks. The weapon is meticulously maintained internally despite external grime—users know this platform's reliability depends on clean barrel linings.
